prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1417; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a collision at an intersection while turning left across oncoming traffic, and the other driver was also at the scene when I arrived.

Entry 2: The driver of the insured vehicle is listed on the policy, and I confirmed the coverage was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: Police attended and their report places the insured vehicle in the intersection with the other vehicle, and a responding officer noted the claimant was seated inside the car.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the sequence the insured described, with the left turn and the oncoming car's approach.

Entry 5: Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front of the insured vehicle and the side of the other car, which fits the angle of impact described.

Entry 6: The other driver's account lines up with the insured's on the main facts of the collision, and neither party has offered a conflicting version.

Entry 7: I inspected the vehicle and found the damage is largely consistent with the impact described, with no sign of earlier repairs or prior collision damage that I could identify.

Entry 8: No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the prior claims history, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 9: The claimant has retained a lawyer, who has asked that all further contact go through their office, and I have logged that instruction.

Entry 10: The claimant reported a knee injury and the medical records describe an injury that fits the type and force of the crash, with no prior treatment to that body area on file.

Entry 11: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of knee injury, and I have requested the treating provider's notes to understand the progress.

Entry 12: The claimant has since provided small additional details about the moments before the impact, but the core account has stayed the same across every statement taken so far.
